newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt market strengthens on CPI, Germany.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt market strengthens on CPI, Germany.

text.p: Sweden's debt market drew strength on Tuesday morning from an unchanged CPI in July and the Bundesbank's decision to leave rates unchanged.
Dealers said crown weakness was the only slightly restraining factor in the market.
"If the crown hadn't seemed so tired, yields would have fallen by an additinal two to four basis points," one dealer said.
A lower than expected CPI for July reinforced the positive sentiment created when the German central bank decided against a rate hike. The German spread narrowed four basis points.
CPI in July came out flat against expectations of a rise by 0.1 percent. This gave a year inflation rise of 1.0 percent against expectations of 1.2 percent.
Six month T-bill rates fell two basis points to 4.33 percent and the ten year bond yield fell nine basis points to 6.54 percent.
The crown softened asr foreigners sold crowns against marks.

"We saw a large deal from London of about 300 million marks and it takes some time for the market to absorb such a large deal unless the Riksbank or some other player has an opposite interest," one dealer said.
The crown softened to 4.3865 to the mark versus 4.3785 late Monday.
One dealer said the crown would trade between 4.37 and 4.40 crowns against the mark over the rest of the day.
The market's next focus is the FOMC-meeting.
